text:
elena: heads-up: we9re seeing sustained NIC-level TX retries on host-rack-72 (us-east-2) that push several fractional dedicated slices into soft-fallback and blow past our cross-AZ budget. noticing ~6k retried packets/min.

mike: charts look like a periodic 3-5s microburst every 2m. grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/egress?var-host=host-rack-72&from=now-4h

rashid: can you paste ethtool and /proc/interrupts? also whether this is bonded LACP or active-backup?

elena: quick dumps:
```
cat /proc/interrupts | head -n 8
eth0: tx_errors 0 tx_dropped 0
eth1: tx_errors 142 tx_dropped 12
bond0: lacp_slave1 up, lacp_slave2 up
```

elena: bond0 active-backup, but eth1 is the tenant-egress interface for some dedicated slices. errors only on eth1 during tenant V spikes.

zoe: infra-bot created INC-8511 and notified oncall. :rotating_light: Agree we should protect SLOs first.

infra-bot: [AUDIT] INC-8511 opened by elena (priority P2).

mike: quick mitigation options: 1) steer affected tenants to warm-dedicated-us-east-2-highprio, 2) flip bond to use eth0 for tenant-egress temporarily (risk control-plane churn), 3) enable per-slice rate-limit on eth1 via tc. Which do we prefer?

rashid: prefer (1) then (3). Flipping bond is risky during production traffic. Steer is reversible and cheap.

elena: agree. will run steer for 20m. command:
```
./bin/routectl steer --tenant V --to warm-dedicated-us-east-2-highprio --ttl 1200 --reason "eth1 tx retries causing fallback"
```

infra-bot: [AUDIT] routectl steer invoked by elena for tenant V -> warm-dedicated-us-east-2-highprio TTL=1200

mike: also add a short tc tbf on eth1 for the tenant VF interfaces to smooth bursts while steer is live:
```
tc qdisc add dev vf3 root tbf rate 300mbit burst 128k latency 100ms
```

zoe: costs-bot: what9s the incremental cost for steering V to that warm-dedicated pool for 20m?

costs-bot: Estimated incremental cost: $0.85 for 20-minute window (warm-dedicated multiplier x2.8). Notified billing owners.

rashid: post-steer: I'm still seeing eth1 tx_errors but no route fallbacks. initial suspicion: NIC MSI affinity + LACP transmit hashing causes uneven TX load. Could we try changing tx hashing temporarily to better balance across slaves?

mike: possible command (risky):
```
echo 1 > /sys/class/net/bond0/bond_xmit_hash_policy
```

elena: lets avoid altering bond policy live. Plan: 1) steer (done), 2) apply tc smoothing, 3) capture pcap + ethtool -S + irq snapshot, 4) repro in bench with synthetic fanout and test tx-hash policy.

infra-bot: [NOTICE] steer applied; monitoring window started (20m). Will auto-revert if stable.

rashid: scheduler-bot, can you mark host-rack-72 with label "vf-noisy=true" so scheduler avoids new multi-tenant VF placements pending follow-up?

scheduler-bot: [ACTION] label applied: host-rack-72 -> vf-noisy=true. Allocation heuristics adjusted to prefer 1:1 VF carveouts on labeled hosts.

elena: thanks. I'll attach artifacts to INC-8511 and open an RFC for long-term: either SR-IOV strict carveouts on high-risk racks or automated per-host tx-shaping. Need CAPEX/OPEX comparison.

zoe: tagging @finance. Also can we run a quick simulation of impact if 15% of hosts get SR-IOV strict? scheduler-bot?

scheduler-bot: queued simulation. ETA ~6h. Will post results in INC-8511.

mike: update: after steer + tc, route fallbacks stopped and client-side p95 stabilized. leaving steer live and will capture full trace. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
